history.period: Established 1948 (per boroktimes.com; founder Ven. Dharmavara Mahathera - verify)
history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. Benuban Vihar (also spelt Venuban/Venuvan Vihar) is a BUDDHIST monastery and shrine in the Kunjaban area of Agartala, serving the Chakma/Mog Buddhist community. It houses metal idols of the Buddha and Bodhisattvas said to have been made in Myanmar (Burma) and transported here, and is also called the Buddha Shrine. Reported founded in 1948 by Venerable Dharmavara Mahathera (single source - verify). Buddha Purnima is celebrated with great fervour and a fair; the Vaishakhi Buddha Purnima event in May 2025 was attended by Tripura CM Manik Saha. Coordinates below are Agartala city-centre (the vihara is ~2 km away in Kunjaban) - exact shrine coords unpublished (verify).

name: Benuban Vihar (Venuban Buddha Vihar, Agartala)
town: Agartala (Kunjaban area, ~2 km from city centre)
town_description: Agartala is the capital of Tripura in West Tripura district, on the Haora river near the Bangladesh border; it was the capital of the Manikya kingdom and hosts the Ujjayanta Palace, Kunjaban Palace and several historic shrines. Kunjaban, in northern Agartala, also houses the Kunjaban Palace (the Governor's residence).
tradition: Buddhism (Theravada) - monastery and shrine (NOT a Hindu temple)

travel.airport: Maharaja Bir Bikram Airport, Agartala - about 12 km (verify).
travel.road: Kunjaban area, about 2 km from Agartala city centre; buses stop at Jogendranagar, plus taxis (verify).
